rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour's quake is tremendous; describing the earth as convulsed and using indefinite رجا stresses an indescribably severe shaking.
rows.anchor: وقد عظمها في هذه الآية حيث عبر عنها برج الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about the earth's shaking is appositional to, or explanatory of, “when the Event occurs.”
rows.anchor: والجملة بدل أو بيان لقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-bass is crushing a body into tiny, disintegrating pieces, like fine flour.
rows.anchor: والبس الفت وهو عود الجسم بدق ونحوه أجزاء صغارا متلاشية كالدقيق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes al-bass to mean setting the mountains in motion, as in the verse about the mountains being moved.
rows.anchor: وقيل البس هو التسيير فهو في معنى قوله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported explanation says hiba is dust.
rows.anchor: الهباء قيل هو الغبار وقيل هو الذرة من الغبار

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation identifies hiba as tiny dust particles visible in a sunbeam entering through an opening.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو الذرة من الغبار الظاهر في شعاع الشمس الداخل من كوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inbithath means scattering; the resulting sense is clear.
rows.anchor: والانبثات التفرق، والمعنى ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here zawj means a class or category, and the address is to all human beings.
rows.anchor: الزوج بمعنى الصنف والخطاب لعامة البشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The right-hand group are the fortunate and blessed, contrasted with the left-hand group, who suffer misery and ill fortune.
rows.anchor: أصحاب السعادة واليمن مقابل أصحاب المشأمة أصحاب الشقاء والشؤم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposed sense “people on the right side” is rejected: the contrast would naturally say “people of the left,” not أصحاب المشأمة.
rows.anchor: يرده مقابلة أصحاب الميمنة بأصحاب المشأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما is interrogative and the subject; أصحاب الميمنة is its predicate, while the whole clause predicates the preceding أصحاب الميمنة.
rows.anchor: وما في قوله { ما أصحاب الميمنة } استفهامية ومبتدأ خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question magnifies the right-hand group's importance and status.
rows.anchor: وفي الاستفهام إعظام لأمرهم وتفخيم لشأنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mash'ama is a verbal noun like shu'm, the opposite of yumn; here the pair denotes felicity and misery.
rows.anchor: المشأمة مصدر كالشؤم مقابل اليمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first occurrence refers to those foremost in good deeds, as in the verse classifying people by their deeds and God's leave.
rows.anchor: الذي يصلح أن يفسر به السابقون الأول قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those foremost in good works also precede others toward the forgiveness and mercy corresponding to those works.
rows.anchor: وإذا سبقوا بالخيرات سبقوا إلى المغفرة والرحمة التي بإزائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated expression can be parsed as a subject followed by its predicate.
rows.anchor: وقوله { والسابقون السابقون } مبتدأ وخبر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another parse makes the first السابقون the subject, the second an emphatic repetition, and “those are the brought-near” the predicate.
rows.anchor: وقيل الأول مبتدأ والثاني تأكيد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported reading treats the second word as a restatement of the first, like the quoted Arabic saying about Abu al-Najm and his poetry.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالسابقون الثاني هو الأول على حد قوله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported view identifies them as people who hasten to everything God calls them to do.
rows.anchor: فقيل هم المسارعون إلى كل ما دعا الله إليه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies them as those who enter faith and obedience without delay.
rows.anchor: وقيل هم الذين سبقوا إلى الإيمان والطاعة من غير توان

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view takes them to be the prophets, who preceded the followers of their religions.
rows.anchor: وقيل هم الأنبياء عليهم السلام لأنهم مقدموا أهل الأديان

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view names the believer from Pharaoh's family, Habib al-Najjar, and Ali, first to believe in the Prophet and the best of them.
rows.anchor: وقيل هم مؤمن آل فرعون وحبيب النجار المذكور في سورة يس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other reported identifications are those who preceded in the Hijra.
rows.anchor: وقيل هم السابقون إلى الهجرة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported identification is those who preceded others in the five daily prayers.
rows.anchor: وقيل هم السابقون إلى الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies them as those who prayed toward both qiblas.
rows.anchor: وقيل هم الذين صلوا إلى القبلتين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported identification is those who were first to jihad.
rows.anchor: وقيل هم السابقون إلى الجهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first two additional explanations fit the earlier general sense; prophets and named exemplars should be understood illustratively, as may the remaining identifications.
rows.anchor: والقولان الأولان راجعان إلى ما تقدم من المعنى

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri says Ali ibn al-Husayn likened this world and the next to balancing scales, then explained the Event as Resurrection lowering God's enemies into Hell and raising His friends to Paradise.
rows.anchor: في الخصال عن الزهري قال سمعت علي بن الحسين عليه السلام يقول

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummi says the Event is the certain Resurrection and glosses “lowering” as God's enemies and “raising” as His friends.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي { إذا وقعت الواقعة ليس لوقعتها كاذبة } قال القيامة هي حق

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummi explains the earth's shaking as parts of it striking against one another.
rows.anchor: أولياء الله { إذا رجت الأرض رجا } قال يدق بعضها على بعض

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummi glosses the mountains' crushing as their being uprooted.
rows.anchor: { وبست الجبال بسا } قال قلعت الجبال قلعا

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummi identifies hiba as the dust visible in a sunbeam entering through an opening.
rows.anchor: { فكانت هباء منبثا } قال الهباء الذي في الكوة من شعاع الشمس

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummi glosses the three classes and calls the foremost those who preceded to Paradise; Tabataba'i says this explains the second occurrence of السابقون.
rows.anchor: وقوله { وكنتم أزواجا ثلاثة } قال يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali distinguishes scattered hiba as particle dust and dispersed hiba as sunlight dust seen in a shaft of light.
rows.anchor: وفي الدر المنثور أخرج عبد بن حميد وابن جرير وابن المنذر عن علي بن أبي طالب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the verse was revealed about Hizqil, the believer from Pharaoh's family, Habib al-Najjar, and Ali; each led his people, and Ali was foremost.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن مردويه عن ابن عباس في قوله

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Ja'far names four forerunners: Adam's murdered son, Pharaoh's believer, Habib from Jesus's community, and Ali for Muhammad's community; al-Sadiq is also reported with this account.
rows.anchor: وفي المجمع عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال السابقون أربعة ابن آدم المقتول

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: In a report from Ibn Abbas, the Prophet says Gabriel identified the verse with Ali and his Shi'a, who precede to Paradise and are brought near through God's honor.
rows.anchor: بإسناده إلى ابن عباس قال سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Ja'far says, “We are the foremost, and we are the last ones.”
rows.anchor: وفي كمال الدين بإسناده إلى خيثمة الجعفي عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في حديث

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: A report in al-Uyun transmitted from Ali says that “the foremost, the foremost; those are the brought-near” was revealed concerning him.
rows.anchor: وفي العيون في باب ما جاء عن الرضا عليه السلام من الأخبار المجموعة بإسناده عن علي عليه السلام قال

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Al-Majma' reports an interpretation from Ali that the foremost are those who preceded to the five daily prayers.
rows.anchor: وفي المجمع في الآية وقيل إلى الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabataba'i says these reports should all be read as illustrative instances of the general meaning.
rows.anchor: أقول الوجه حمل جميع هذه الأخبار على التمثيل كما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses begin detailing the outcome on the Resurrection for each of the three classes just named.
rows.anchor: بيان الآيات تفصل ما ينتهي إليه حال كل واحد من الأزواج الثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أولئك points back to the foremost group.
rows.anchor: الإشارة بأولئك إلى السابقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred parse makes أولئك المقربون a new subject-predicate sentence, fitting the passage's division of humanity followed by each group's outcome.
rows.anchor: وأول الوجوه الثلاثة أوجه بالنظر إلى سياق تقسيم الناس إلى ثلاثة أزواج

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One alternative makes the clause the predicate of والسابقون.
rows.anchor: وقيل خبر لقوله { والسابقون }

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another parse treats أولئك as the subject and في جنات النعيم as its predicate.
rows.anchor: وقيل مبتدأ خبره في جنات النعيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nearness and distance first describe bodies by spatial relation, then extend to time and other comparisons, and finally to nonphysical realities.
rows.anchor: والقرب والبعد معنيان متضائفان تتصف بهما الأجسام بحسب النسبة المكانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's nearness describes His encompassing all things; being nearer to a thing than it is to itself is the most remarkable conception of nearness.
rows.anchor: وقد اعتبر القرب وصفا له تعالى بما له من الإحاطة بكل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A servant approaches God through good works by entering the reach of divine mercy as causes of misery and deprivation fall away; God brings the servant near by granting special honor, forgiveness, and mercy.
rows.anchor: فالعبد يتقرب بصالح العمل إلى الله سبحانه وهو وقوعه في معرض شمول الرحمة الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brought-near are the highest rank of the blessed, as the link to the foremost indicates; attaining this rank requires complete servitude.
rows.anchor: فالمقربون هم النمط الأعلى من أهل السعادة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Ibn Mardawayh reports from Abu Hurayra that Companions grieved at “few from later people,” then a later revelation said both groups were numerous and, they thought, abrogated the first verse.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن مردويه عن أبي هريرة قال لما نزلت

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf rejects the abrogation report: the first and second passages plainly concern different groups, and abrogation in reports is impossible.
rows.anchor: قال في الكشاف في تفسير الآية فإن قلت فقد روي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reconciliation says Companions mistook their community as having few saved people and the later verse removed that assumption; Tabataba'i finds this unsupported and contrary to the wording, especially the proposed sense of abrogation.
rows.anchor: وأنت خبير بأنه حمل على ما لا دليل عليه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Al-Majma' reports a view that these youths are children who had neither good nor evil deeds and were assigned this station.
rows.anchor: وفي المجمع في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet answered that children of polytheists serve the people of Paradise; Tabataba'i notes its transmission from Hasan and grades it weak and unreliable.
rows.anchor: وقد روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أنه سئل

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reports that the Prophet said a desired bird in Paradise falls before one already roasted; other reports say eaten food returns to life and flies back to its place.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي الدنيا في صفة الجنة والبزار وابن مردويه والبيهقي في البعث عن عبد الله بن مسعود

words: لا يسمعون فيها لغوا ولا تأثيما
rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummi glosses the sounds absent in Paradise as obscenity, lies, and singing.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى

words: لا يسمعون فيها لغوا ولا تأثيما
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabataba'i suggests that “singing” may mean entertainment singing, or that the word is a copyist's corruption of khana, obscenity.
rows.anchor: أقول لعل المراد بالغنا ما يكون منه لهوا أو الغنا مصحف الخنا

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummi identifies the people of the right as Ali and his companions.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report applies “right” to the true Imam, Ali, and his followers; Tabataba'i calls this an instance of the verse's general application (jary), based on 17:71.
rows.anchor: الرواية مبنية على ما ورد في ذيل قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummi describes the lote tree as lacking leaves and thorns.
rows.anchor: وفيه في قوله تعالى { في سدر مخضود } شجر لا يكون له ورق

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abu Abd Allah is reported to have read طلع منضود and explained it as fruit piled one upon another.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عبد الله عليه السلام { وطلع منضود } قال بعضه على بعض

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Abu Umama reports that a Bedouin objected that lote trees have thorns; the Prophet said God removes them, replacing each with fruit yielding 72 unlike kinds of food. Al-Hakim authenticated the report.
rows.anchor: وفي الدر المنثور أخرج الحاكم وصححه والبيهقي في البعث عن أبي أمامة

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: A report says a man recited طلح منضود before Ali, who corrected it to طلع by comparison with the verse about palm spathes; he declined to alter the Qur'an publicly.
rows.anchor: وفي المجمع وروت العامة عن علي عليه السلام أنه قرأ رجل عنده

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali is reported to explain طلح منضود as bananas.
rows.anchor: وفي الدر المنثور أخرج عبد الرزاق والفاريابي وهناد

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majma' reports that a rider could travel a hundred years beneath a tree's shade, citing “extended shade”; Tabataba'i notes parallel reports from Abu Sa'id, Anas, and others from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وفي المجمع ورد في الخبر أن في الجنة شجرة يسير الراكب

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Another report says Paradise's times resemble summer mornings, without heat or cold.
rows.anchor: وروي أيضا أن أوقات الجنة كغدوات الصيف لا يكون فيها حر ولا برد

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet describes the people of Paradise visiting one another in their gardens under extended shade, for a period like dawn to sunrise and even more pleasant.
rows.anchor: وفي روضة الكافي بإسناده عن علي بن إبراهيم

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummi says the newly created beings are the houris of Paradise and glosses عربا as speaking only Arabic.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي وقوله { إنا أنشأناهن إنشاء } قال الحور العين في الجنة

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet, transmitted through Ja'far al-Sadiq from his father, says their speech is Arabic.
rows.anchor: وفي الدر المنثور أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن جعفر بن محمد عن أبيه قال قال رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reports understand عربا as the plural of عروب, an affectionate or coquettish woman, rather than a reference to Arabic speech.
rows.anchor: أقول وفيه روايات أخر أن عربا جمع عروب وهي الغنجة

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A sound-chain report from Abu Bakra says both groups are from this community; Tabataba'i says the surah's apparent division concerns all humanity, so such reports may identify instances, though that is far-fetched.
rows.anchor: بسند حسن عن أبي بكرة عن النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent scope is humanity as a whole, not Muhammad's community alone; community-specific narrations may give particular instances, but Tabataba'i finds that reading remote.
rows.anchor: لكن ظاهر آيات السورة أن القسمة لكافة البشر لا لهذه الأمة خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports that the people of the right are Ali's followers, and the people of the left his family's enemies, are likewise taken as identifying particular instances.
rows.anchor: وكذا المراد مما ورد أن أصحاب اليمين أصحاب أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Mu'awiya ibn Wahb reports that al-Sadiq disliked drinking in one breath and glossed الهيم as camels.
rows.anchor: وفي المحاسن بإسناده عن معاوية بن وهب عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Halabi reports that al-Sadiq disliked imitating the الهيم and glossed the word as sand.
rows.anchor: وفيه بإسناده عن الحلبي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both reported senses of الهيم, camels and sand, also occur in other narrations.
rows.anchor: أقول والمعنيان جميعا واردان في روايات أخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wabal is the evil consequence of an affair; the affair here is their unbelief and the transgression that followed from it.
rows.anchor: وبال الأمر تبعته السيئة والمراد بأمرهم كفرهم وما تفرع عليه من فسوقهم

words: ألم يأتكم نبأ الذين كفروا من قبل
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's names and attributes entail resurrection and judgment, which require revealed law; messengers convey it with warning and glad tidings. The passage moves from past disbelievers to rejection of revelation, then denial of resurrection, before faith and final reward or punishment.
rows.anchor: لما كان مقتضى أسمائه الحسنى وصفاته العليا المعدودة في الآيات السابقة وجوب معاد الناس

words: ألم يأتكم نبأ الذين كفروا من قبل
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to polytheists and alludes to destroyed earlier peoples such as Noah's, 'Ad's, and Thamud's communities.
rows.anchor: الخطاب للمشركين وفيه إشارة إلى قصص الأمم السالفة الهالكة كقوم نوح وعاد وثمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their evil consequence was annihilating punishment in this life; the painful punishment is in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى ما نزل عليهم من عذاب الاستئصال

words: ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُۥ كَانَت تَّأْتِيهِمْ رُسُلُهُم بِٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next verse identifies rejection of the messengers as the cause of both the worldly annihilation and the afterlife punishment just mentioned.
rows.anchor: بيان لسبب ما ذكر من تعذيبهم بعذاب الاستئصال وعذاب الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The independent clause begins without a coordinating conjunction, answering an implied question about why they suffered; ذلك points to the punishments just described.
rows.anchor: ولذلك جيء بالفصل دون العطف كأنه جواب لسؤال مقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect with كانت portrays messengers' repeated arrival, while the contrasted wording presents their rejection as one decisive, stubborn refusal.
rows.anchor: وفي التعبير عن إتيان الرسل ودعوتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pattern matches earlier communities who would not believe what they had already rejected; God seals the hearts of disbelievers and transgressors.
rows.anchor: تلك القرى نقص عليك من أنبائها ولقد جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bashar can be singular or plural; here it is plural, as shown by the following plural verb يهدوننا.
rows.anchor: يطلق البشر على الواحد والجمع والمراد به الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite بشر belittles the messengers, while the question rejects the idea that mere humans with no superiority over them could guide them; this reflects arrogance.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام للإنكار أي قالوا على سبيل الإنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their contemptuous objection led them to base disbelief and turning away on that claim.
rows.anchor: ولذلك فرع تعالى على قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For God, who is rich in Himself, istighna means manifesting self-sufficiency rather than acquiring wealth.
rows.anchor: الاستغناء طلب الغنى وهو من الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that people imagined their knowledge, strength, and ability guaranteed their survival; their extermination manifested God's independence from their existence.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنهم كانوا يرون أن لهم من العلم والقوة والاستطاعة ما يدفع عن جمعهم الفناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: More broadly, people presume God owes them happiness and favor; worldly consequences and afterlife punishment together show His independence from them.
rows.anchor: فالمراد باستغنائه تعالى عنهم مجموع ما أفيد بقوله { فذاقوا وبال أمرهم ولهم عذاب أليم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabataba'i offers two related readings and judges the second broader; either way, the word conveys God's majesty and power.
rows.anchor: فهذان وجهان في معنى قوله تعالى { واستغنى الله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destruction exemplifies successive missions that nations rejected, leaving them as tales of the past.
rows.anchor: ثم أرسلنا رسلنا تترا كلما جاء أمة رسولها كذبوه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One alternative says God needed no further guidance after establishing proof and completing the argument.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد واستغنى الله بإقامة البرهان وإتمام الحجة عليهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another alternative says God has always been independent of their obedience and worship.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد واستغنى الله عن طاعتهم وعبادتهم أزلا وأبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabataba'i dismisses the proof-sufficiency and worship-independence alternatives.
rows.anchor: والوجهان كما ترى. وقوله { والله غني حميد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing clause explains the judgment: God is intrinsically rich and praiseworthy in His acts; just punishment returns people's own deeds to them.
rows.anchor: في محل التعليل لمضمون الآية، والمعنى والله غني في ذاته

words: زعم الذين كفروا أن لن يبعثوا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Denial of resurrection is another pillar of idolatrous disbelief; without it, divine religion's commands, prohibitions, judgment, and recompense would have no effect, also undermining the rationale for messengership.
rows.anchor: ذكر ركن آخر من أركان كفر الوثنيين وهو إنكارهم الدين السماوي بإنكار المعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazahur means mutual cooperation; وإن تظاهرا is contracted from وإن تتظاهرا.
rows.anchor: التظاهر التعاون، وأصل { وإن تظاهرا } وإن تتظاهرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The separating pronoun stresses God's special care for the Prophet, supporting and managing his affairs without an intermediary from creation.
rows.anchor: وضمير الفصل في قوله { فإن الله هو مولاه } للدلالة على أن لله سبحانه عناية خاصة به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawla here means the guardian who takes charge of the Prophet's affairs and helps him against anyone seeking him harm.
rows.anchor: والمولى الولي الذي يتولى أمره وينصره على من يريده بسوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both Gabriel and صالح المؤمنين are coordinated with the name of God.
rows.anchor: و { جبريل } عطف على لفظ الجلالة، و { صالح المؤمنين } عطف كجبريل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view takes صالح المؤمنين collectively as the righteous believers, using a singular form with a generic sense; Tabataba'i notes that the construct differs in form from الصالح من المؤمنين.
rows.anchor: والمراد بصالح المؤمنين على ما قيل الصلحاء من المؤمنين فصالح المؤمنين واحد أريد به الجمع

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Sunni reports from the Prophet and Shi'i reports from the Imams identify صالح المؤمنين specifically as Ali; Tabataba'i sets aside other proposed identifications for lack of evidence.
rows.anchor: ووردت الرواية من طرق أهل السنة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ومن طرق الشيعة عن أئمة أهل البيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular predicate ظهير presents the angels as united in support, one aligned rank.
rows.anchor: إفراد الخبر للدلالة على أنهم متفقون في نصره متحدون صفا واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning the angels after God's guardianship, Gabriel, and صالح المؤمنين magnifies the Prophet's support.
rows.anchor: وفي جعلهم بعد ذلك أي بعد ولاية الله وجبريل وصالح المؤمنين تعظيم وتفخيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah repeatedly establishes God's support for the Prophet and rebukes those opposing him; shifts among the Prophet, believers, and wives reveal the episode only after his vindication is secured.
rows.anchor: ولحن الآيات في إظهار النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم على من يؤذيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening rebuke for forbidding himself what God made lawful and the direction to release his oath function as support and vindication despite their rebuke form.
rows.anchor: وقد خوطب فيها النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أولا وعوتب على تحريمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address shifts from believers to the Prophet's wives and alludes obliquely to the story after first establishing support for him.
rows.anchor: ثم التفت من خطابه إلى خطاب المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wives' hearts had strayed; they face a choice to repent or align against the Prophet despite God's, Gabriel's, the righteous believers', and the angels' support, followed by hope that God replace them with better wives if he divorces them.
rows.anchor: وقرر أن قلوبهما قد صغت بما فعلتا ولم يأمرهما أن تتوبا من ذنبهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After this exchange, the surah commands the Prophet to strive against disbelievers and hypocrites, then gives paired examples for disbelievers and believers.
rows.anchor: ثم أمر النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يجاهد الكفار والمنافقين

words: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ قُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَكُمْ وَأَهْلِيكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage alternates between believers protecting themselves and families, disbelievers told not to excuse themselves, believers told to repent, and the Prophet told to fight disbelievers and hypocrites.
rows.anchor: فقال { يا أيها الذين آمنوا قوا أنفسكم وأهليكم } الخ
